data.title: Forgent projects $2.4B-$2.6B fiscal 2027 revenue as it expands Powertrain Solutions capacity in Tijuana
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Forgent Power Solutions (FPS) Q4 2026

Management View

  • "We closed fiscal 2026 with the strongest quarter in Forgent's history, delivering record quarterly revenues, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted net income." (CEO & Director Gary Niederpruem)

  • "Fourth quarter revenues increased 94% to a record $462 million" and "adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 200 basis points sequentially to 24.4%." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • "We also booked more than $1.5 billion of orders in the quarter alone" and "today, our backlog stands at $3 billion." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • "We received our first direct order from a Frontier AI lab in the fourth quarter, and we have also signed an MSA with the hyperscaler." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • "Today, we announced an incremental investment to build a dedicated 385,000 square foot Powertrain Solutions facility in our Tijuana, Mexico campus" and "we expect the new facility to come online in the fourth quarter of fiscal '27." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • "Fourth quarter revenues were $462 million, up 94% year-over-year and 22% sequentially" and "all of that growth was organic." (Chief Financial Officer Ryan Fiedler)

Outlook

  • "We expect revenue of $2.4 billion to $2.6 billion" and "we expect adjusted EBITDA of $575 million to $625 million." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • "We also expect adjusted EPS of $1.26 to $1.40" and "we expect adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 24%, up from 22.7% in fiscal '26." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • "Today, we are providing guidance for the first quarter of fiscal '27" with "Q1 revenues of $445 million to $465 million and adjusted EBITDA of $90 million to $100 million," including "approximately $10 million of one-time costs." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • "We will no longer report orders and backlog on a quarterly basis" and "we will begin providing quarterly revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance for the next fiscal quarter on a rolling basis." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

Financial Results

  • "Revenues increased $667 million or 89% to $1.42 billion" and "adjusted EBITDA increased $154 million or 91% to $323 million." (Chief Financial Officer Fiedler)

  • "Powertrain Solutions revenues increased 187% to $147 million" and "custom Products revenues increased 73% to $292 million." (Chief Financial Officer Fiedler)

  • "Gross profit increased 109% on volume growth and favorable product mix" and "SG&A increased in absolute dollars... but declined as a percentage of sales as revenue growth outpaced operated cost growth." (Chief Financial Officer Fiedler)

  • "Operating cash flow increased approximately 2.5x in fiscal '26 to $109 million from $45 million in fiscal '25" and "we expect another substantial step-up in fiscal '27 with operating cash flow of more than $300 million." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

Q&A

  • Andrew Obin, BofA Securities: Backlog quality, pricing, and conversion timing? CEO & Director Niederpruem: "Anything in our backlog is a firm purchase order" and "pricing remains very consistent... There isn't any great swings up or down from what we saw over the prior quarter."

  • Julien Dumoulin-Smith, Jefferies: Margin ramp through fiscal '27 and longer-term trajectory? Chief Financial Officer Fiedler: "The first quarter, we're coming in at about 21%" and "we do expect some strong operating leverage and improving margins... 24% for the full year."

  • Michael Elias, TD Cowen: Potential long-term capacity agreements with hyperscalers and the cost to set up? CEO & Director Niederpruem: "There is dialogue... around anything from individual POs all the way to making longer-term commitments" and "we think we have that covered in the plan that we've laid out today."

  • Luke Junk, Baird: Powertrain Solutions at "approximately 40%" of backlog and durability vs incumbents? CEO & Director Niederpruem: "The outsized growth has come from increasing... revenue per customer" and customers "are now selling those customers either multiple product lines or selling them integrated solutions."

  • Joseph Ritchie, Goldman Sachs: Why expand Powertrain Solutions capacity now and why Tijuana? CEO & Director Niederpruem: "Powertrain Solutions... seems to be the dominant deployment mechanism" and "it's the right thing to do now to stay ahead of the curve so we can keep those lead times inside of the market expected lead times."

  • Chigusa Katoku, JPMorgan: Margin implications as Powertrain Solutions mix rises and complexity/supply chain? CEO & Director Niederpruem: "The margin profile... is all sort of still within a standard deviation" and noted some solutions may include "third-party gear" where "you can't mark up as much as you with your own organic content."

  • Noah Kaye, Oppenheimer: M&A focus areas and financial criteria? CEO & Director Niederpruem: "Service is very clearly at the top of their list" and "it has to be both a strategic fit and past the financial parameters."

  • David Tarantino, KeyBanc (for Jeff): Reliance on ramping labor and supply chain to deliver the guide? CEO & Director Niederpruem: "We've demonstrated that we can hire... hundreds and hundreds and hundreds of people of every quarter" and "there isn't anything habitual" in supply chain beyond needing to "manage it."

  • Nigel Coe, Wolfe: Lead times advantage and constraints over the next 6-12 months? CEO & Director Niederpruem: "We still do believe that we are inside the expected lead times for every product line" and highlighted "massive training dojos in every one of our facilities."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly positive, with repeated probing on demand durability, backlog quality, margin cadence, lead times, and execution capacity, alongside supportive phrasing such as "Nicely done" (Julien Dumoulin-Smith, Jefferies) and "Kudos" (Joseph Ritchie, Goldman Sachs).

  • Management: positive in prepared remarks and steady in Q&A, using definitive language including "backlog is 100% firm commitments" and "we are not seeing" meaningful pushouts. (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • Versus last quarter: management continued confidence but introduced more explicit process changes and scaling signals, including "we will no longer report orders and backlog on a quarterly basis" and increased emphasis on "beginning to look outward at acquisition opportunities" in fiscal '27. (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The current call added a larger strategic expansion announcement and timing: "build a dedicated 385,000 square foot Powertrain Solutions facility" that is expected to be online "in the fourth quarter of fiscal '27." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • Guidance visibility language strengthened: in Q4, management said "our backlog covers more than 90% of our revenue guidance"; in Q3, management emphasized backlog was "nearly $2 billion" and that it "provides strong visibility into future revenue." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • Disclosure approach shifted: Q4 stated "we will no longer report orders and backlog on a quarterly basis," while Q3 highlighted quarterly "record bookings" and "book-to-bill" as core visibility metrics. (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • Q&A focus broadened from Q3 themes such as tariffs and inflation protection to Q4 themes centered on backlog quality, margin ramp sequencing, capacity agreements with hyperscalers, and M&A parameters. (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

Risks and Concerns

  • "A significant portion of our backlog is scheduled for delivery in Q2, Q3 and Q4" and revenue is expected to be "more heavily weighted towards those quarters than Q1." (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • "In Q1, that will translate to approximately $10 million of one-time costs" tied to "investments early in the year" ahead of a production ramp. (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

  • Execution capacity remains a recurring topic: "every quarter, we're going to have to continue to add hundreds of employees" and management positioned training and hiring as the core mitigation. (CEO & Director Niederpruem)

Final Takeaway

Forgent’s management framed Q4 as a record quarter and positioned fiscal 2027 around scaling into modular Powertrain Solutions, direct engagement with hyperscalers and Frontier AI labs, and a shift toward cash generation and M&A. The company guided to $2.4 billion to $2.6 billion of fiscal 2027 revenue and introduced a new disclosure cadence that ends quarterly orders/backlog reporting, while highlighting that backlog covers more than 90% of the year’s revenue outlook and that a new 385,000 square foot Powertrain Solutions facility in Tijuana is expected to come online in fiscal Q4 2027.

data.title: Rock Tech Lithium upsizes private placement to C$6M with strategic backing
data.description:
• Rock Tech Lithium (RCKTF) said on Tuesday that it increased its previously announced non-brokerage private placement to up to C$6M.
  • The company has so far issued 8.17M units for about C$5.31M, including C$3.51M raised in the latest tranche.
  • A strategic investor subscribed to C$3.25M and is expected to enter a strategic equity partnership tied to Rock Tech’s fully permitted Guben lithium hydroxide converter in Germany.
  • Each unit is priced at C$0.65 and includes one common share and half a warrant. Each full warrant allows the holder to buy one additional share at C$0.90 for 36 months.
  • The proceeds will be used to advance the Georgia Lake Mine feasibility study, develop its Red Rock Converter in Ontario, and support general working capital.
  • Separately, the company also appointed Derek Sobel as CFO, replacing Christopher Wright, who is relocating to Australia.
  • The financing remains subject to final TSX Venture Exchange approval.

data.title: U.S. crude stockpiles rose 7.1M barrels last week, API says
data.description:
The American Petroleum Institute reportedly shows a build of 7.14M barrels of oil in U.S. commercial stockpiles for the week ending September 11, after inventories fell by 300K barrels in the previous week.

Gasoline inventories reportedly show a build of 1.46M barrels for the week, distillate inventories reportedly show a build of 1.61M barrels, and Cushing inventories reportedly show a draw of 246K barrels.

The Energy Information Administration is scheduled to release its weekly U.S. petroleum supply report on Wednesday, with the average of analysts surveyed by The Wall Street Journal forecasting domestic commercial crude stocks would fall by 1.4M barrels, while gasoline inventories were expected to decline by 800K barrels and distillate inventories were expected to remain unchanged from the previous week.

WTI front-month September crude oil (CL1:COM) recently traded at $105.48/bbl, after settling Tuesday at $105.83/bbl.

data.title: Lenovo inks MOU with MemryX to expand sovereign edge AI in Saudi Arabia
data.description:
Lenovo (LNVGY) signed a memorandum of understanding with MemryX, a provider of power-efficient, scalable AI technology, to expand the deployment of sovereign edge AI solutions in Saudi Arabia.

The agreement builds on joint platform deployments already operating in the country and establishes a framework for Lenovo and MemryX to pursue additional opportunities across infrastructure, industrial operations, smart cities and video management. The collaboration also supports Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 by enabling organizations to deploy practical AI capabilities while maintaining greater control over their data and computing infrastructure.

The joint platform combines the Lenovo ThinkEdge SE455 V3 rugged edge server with the MemryX Cascade 100P AI accelerator to process video and sensor data on site.

"What matters to customers is being able to do that while keeping their data close to where it's created and under their control," said Salman Faqeeh, Vice President and General Manager, Saudi Arabia, Lenovo. "That's why our work with MemryX is relevant and timely. Together, we're helping bring AI into real-world environments where it can make an immediate difference. What's even more relevant is that this isn't a future concept. We're already seeing this deployment help customers improve safety and efficiency in real operating environments across Saudi Arabia."

data.title: GoldQuest appoints Dennis Kwong as CFO
data.description:
GoldQuest Mining (GQC:CA) announced the appointment of Dennis Kwong as chief financial officer of the company, effective September 15th, 2026.

Most recently, Kwong served as Chief Financial Officer of Florida Canyon Gold, where he assisted in the spinout and public listing of the company as part of the business combination between Argonaut Gold and Alamos Gold (AGI). 

Before Florida Canyon Gold, Kwong spent approximately 15 years with Centerra Gold, where he held positions including executive vice president, business development; vice president, business development and exploration; and Vice President, Business Development. 

Earlier in his career, Kwong held senior business development positions with Xstrata Nickel, Falconbridge, and Noranda. 

Source: press release

data.title: Gold and silver tick lower ahead of Fed rate decision
data.description:
Gold and silver futures settled modestly lower in cautious trading Tuesday, a day ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision, which is widely expected to be a quarter-point rate increase to the 3.75%-4.0% range with further ​tightening signaled.

The continued rally in crude oil prices fueled inflation worries and reinforced expectations that the Fed will raise rates, while benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yields rose to their highest level ​since 2007, and the dollar rose, making greenback-priced bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies.

"Much of the hawkish Fed risk appears ​to be priced in. However, gold could remain vulnerable if policymakers signal ​rates will ⁠stay higher for longer," ING analysts said in a note.

Gold's recent moves suggest little hope that the metal will recapture its role as a haven asset any time soon, TradeNation's David Morrison wrote, as investors have piled back into the dollar and out of gold as the deteriorating Middle East situation and tech leaders' doomsday warnings about AI soured risk sentiment.

Front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) and silver (XAGUSD:CUR) for September delivery both slipped 0.4% to $4,291.60/oz and $63.23/oz, respectively, with both metals posting their lowest settlement values since August 6.

data.title: nVent prices $800M senior notes offering to fund Maverick deal
data.description:
• nVent Electric (NVT) said on Tuesday that its subsidiary Hoffman Schroff priced an $800M offering of 6.150% senior notes due 2036.
  • The deal is expected to close on September 29.
  • nVent and its subsidiaries also plan to raise a $600M three-year term loan and allow up to $250M in additional revolving credit borrowings.
  • The financing, along with cash on hand and potentially a bridge loan, will be used primarily to fund the planned $1.75B acquisition of Maverick Power and related costs.
  • The notes offering is not dependent on the acquisition closing.
  • If the deal does not close by the applicable deadline, the company must redeem the outstanding notes at 101% of principal, plus accrued interest.

data.title: Ashland edges higher on report bids due this month
data.description:
Ashland (ASH) ticked higher by almost 1% amid a report that the chemical maker is collecting takeover bids this month.

Apollo Global (APO) and Carlyle Group (CG) are among the financial sponsors interested in Ashland (ASH), according to traders, who cited a DealReporter article that was circulating on Tuesday.

The update comes after Bloomberg reported last month that the chemical maker was evaluating a possible sale after getting takeover interest. Advent, Apollo, and Carlyle Group (CG) are among those that have had contact with the company.

Standard Industries Inc., which, through its investment platform Standard Investments LLC is among Ashland’s biggest shareholders, is also interested, according to the Bloomberg report.  

A potential deal comes as activist investors have been pushing for months for Ashland (ASH)  to explore a sale. Last month, Ashland confirmed an agreement with activist investor Ancora Holdings to expand the chemical maker's board.

Ashland (ASH) is set to hold its innovation day on Thursday.
